A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VIPO by the same authors. Their main text, equations, algorithms, six tables, four figures, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original VIPO evaluations on D4RL, NeoRL, and Adroit, together with prediction-error experiments, data-removal tests, and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the ablations and Adroit evaluations in Appendices F and G.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2, the augmented loss, value-learning objectives, and practical surrogate gradient in Eq. (11) remain unchanged. v2 explains the approximation behind the existing update without establishing a procedural or architectural change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same D4RL locomotion and Adroit tasks, NeoRL tasks, and Walker2d data-removal scenario. The experimental-setup descriptions move to Appendix E.1.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches in Tables 1, 2, and 6, including COMBO and RAMBO on D4RL and EDAC on NeoRL and Adroit. The MOPO uncertainty comparison and original-loss model control are also retained.

E3.justification: Both retain the 9:1 prediction-error split, 1,000 NeoRL trajectories per task, data-removal construction and increments, evaluation metrics, and settings in Tables 4–5. No experimental-protocol revision is reported.

E4.justification: The uncertainty-versus-data-removal experiment, prediction-error comparison, and lambda ablations on four Walker2d datasets are unchanged. Figures 3–4 retain the same model-error and policy-training curves despite relocation.

E5.justification: Both report four random seeds for benchmark returns and Figure 2, and six for Table 3's model errors. The same uncertainty displays are retained, with no added run-count information or statistical procedure.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–6 match, and Figures 2–4 retain the same plots. VIPO's average returns remain 83.6 on D4RL locomotion, 73.3 on NeoRL, and 25.8 ± 3.7 on Adroit. The rewritten uncertainty discussion introduces no new empirical result.

T1.justification: The central Model Gradient Theorem, renumbered from 3.2 to 3.3, receives substantive corrections. Its discounted-transition definition now starts at t=0 and excludes the initial-distribution factor; the gradient correctly distinguishes the initial state, visited state, and subsequent transition. Appendix B revises the corresponding derivation. Appendix C also adds a short proof of the previously asserted learned-model fixed-point property.

C1.justification: The core value-inconsistency framework and benchmark-performance claims remain. v2 adds an explicit first-of-its-kind claim about incorporating inconsistency during model training and emphasizes comprehensive data use without costly diffusion or transformer architectures.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 adds a small-time-step rationale for the surrogate approximation and a policy-gradient analogy explaining value alignment. Section 4.2.3 removes v1's single-sample variance explanation for MOPO's behavior and adopts a more cautious interpretation of the unchanged uncertainty plot.

D1.justification: v2 newly identifies NVIDIA RTX 4090 GPUs, replaces the anonymous code link with the NUS-CORE/vipo GitHub link, and explicitly documents the tuple approximation underlying Eq. (11). Hyperparameters, training budgets, and baseline-result sources remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Sutton et al. (1999) for the policy-gradient analogy and removes Seo et al. (2020), previously cited in Appendix B. The introduction strengthens novelty and architecture-related positioning, while Appendix A's related-work coverage is otherwise retained.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites affect the introduction, gradient explanation, uncertainty discussion, and conclusion. Experimental setups move from Section 4.1.1 to Appendix E.1, and Appendix H adds an LLM-use declaration. The overall narrative and section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, substantially reflowing equations, algorithms, and tables. Figure 1 is redrawn with neural-network diagrams and explicit MSBE/NLL pathways. Figures 3–4, previously sharing a page, are displayed separately; their plotted content is unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects inconsistencies in the central gradient theorem and Appendix B derivation, explains the practical approximation more transparently, and adds useful hardware and code-access information. These provide a clear but limited improvement: the unchanged surrogate update still relies on an informal small-time-step argument, so the revision does not fully resolve the gap between the exact theorem and practical optimization.
